discovery: Realization and exploration of strongly interacting Fermi gases and fermionic superfluidity across the BEC-BCS crossover

nominees.name: Rudolf Grimm
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Christophe Salomon
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire Kastler Brossel, Ecole Normale Superieure, Paris, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / ultracold quantum gases
motivation: Using magnetically tunable Feshbach resonances in ultracold lithium-6, the nominees turned a dilute atomic gas into the cleanest strongly correlated fermionic system known. Thomas first produced a strongly interacting, unitary Fermi gas (2002) and showed its hydrodynamic, near-perfect-fluid expansion, linking cold atoms to quark-gluon plasma and neutron-star matter. Grimm and Salomon created long-lived weakly bound molecules and Bose-Einstein condensates of molecules from fermions (2003), then continuously connected them to Cooper-paired states, measuring the pairing gap, collective modes and thermodynamics across the BEC-BCS crossover. Salomon's precise equation-of-state measurements made the unitary gas a quantitative benchmark for many-body theory. Together this work established a universal, controllable platform for fermionic superfluidity, bridging superconductivity, nuclear and astrophysical matter, and it underlies today's quantum simulation of Hubbard physics and high-temperature superconductivity models.
